issues.element: Cache-write tokens and Reported reasoning tokens KPI tiles: the r13 'Flat trend' text is now a flat sparkline drawn in neutral grey, while the four other token sparklines are violet. Grey is the duration ink, so these two token tiles read as a different metric family, or as a disabled or no-data placeholder.
issues.fix: Draw flat sparklines in the metric's own ink (violet for tokens) at the same stroke weight as the other sparklines. Pin the line to the baseline, or to the value's real position on a shared 0-based scale, not the vertical middle, so 'flat' does not suggest a mid-range level.

issues.element: Priced events (100) and Unpriced events (28) KPI tiles: flat grey sparklines span the whole tile, where r13 had a 'Flat trend' note. On Overview, counts use white ink and Failed events uses red, so grey here breaks the count = white rule, and two identical grey rules look like dividers, not data.
issues.fix: Use white ink for these event-count sparklines, like Retained events on Overview, and shorten them to the sparkline width used by the cost tile, so they read as trends, not separators.

issues.element: Usage trend (and Token, Cost and Duration trends): smoothed splines between hourly buckets overshoot, adding peaks and troughs that are not in the data. White and violet touch 0 between peaks (around 21:00 and 06:30) and cyan swings between buckets. Hourly aggregates are drawn as continuous curves, but the TTFT chart on Performance uses straight segments, so interpolation is inconsistent.
issues.fix: Use straight (linear) or monotone-cubic interpolation on every trend chart so no curve leaves the range of its bucket values. Add a small point marker per bucket (as the partial 12:00–13:00 segment already has) so readers can see where real values are.

issues.element: KPI row: 'Total tokens 98K' sits beside 'Reported input tokens 3.5B' and 'Reported output tokens 14.5M'. A total smaller than its parts reads as a bug. The usage trend's violet axis (max 80K) also matches the 98K figure, not the 3.5B one.
issues.fix: Say what 'Total tokens' covers in its caption, for example 'Events with full token breakdown', or rename it to that scope. Otherwise drop it from Overview and lead with Reported input tokens.

issues.element: Token trend plots 'Total tokens' as its main series, but this tab has no Total tokens KPI, while Reported input tokens (3.5B, the first tile) is not plotted. Three violet series on three separate axes (80K / 1.2K / 16K) are told apart only by 1px dash and dot swatches.
issues.fix: Plot the series the KPI row leads with (input, output, cache-read), or add a Total tokens tile first. Consider small multiples (one mini chart per series on its own axis) instead of three axes in one plot, which suggests crossings that mean nothing.

issues.element: 'By provider · Estimated cost · USD' shows Claude $1,547.35 and GPT / Codex $1,547.35, each with a full-width bar and each equal to the KPI total. The same happens on Performance (2,400 each) and Tokens (12.5K each). A breakdown that does not add up to its total looks like double counting.
issues.fix: If a breakdown is not a partition, say so in the card caption ('Each provider shown independently; values do not sum to the total'). Otherwise show each provider's actual share and scale the bars against the total, not against the largest row.

issues.element: Explanation card second line 'Legacy cache-write lifetime unavailable' is jargon with no reason or effect, and has no full stop although the sentence above it does. The KPI caption 'Partial' also has no reason.
issues.fix: Rewrite as one sentence, for example 'Cache-write cost is excluded for older events because their cache lifetime was not recorded.' Change the KPI caption to 'Partial: 28 unpriced events excluded'.

issues.element: Toolbar: below about 1366 px, 'Current bucket: hour' disappears and Clear filters collapses to a bare ×. With 'Auto' selected, nothing then says which bucket the chart uses.
issues.fix: Keep the bucket readout at narrow widths, for example as 'Auto (hour)' inside the selected pill, or as a suffix on the chart title ('Usage trend · hourly').

issues.element: KPI row 1: 'p95 execution duration · ms' wraps to two lines, so '2,400' sits about 5 px lower than 128 / 8 / $1,547.35. Row 2: 'Reported output tokens' wraps the same way and drops '14.5M'.
issues.fix: Pin the value row to a fixed offset from the tile top (reserve two label lines, or clamp labels to one line with a title tooltip), so every KPI number shares one baseline.

issues.element: Duration trend: a grey area fill under the p95 line runs to 0 and sits behind the mean line, so a percentile reads like a volume.
issues.fix: Remove the area fill from duration charts. Keep fills for additive quantities (counts, cost) only.

issues.element: Every chart repeats 'Hover or focus a time to compare values; activate it to open matching events.' and 'Gaps are unmeasured periods.' Performance shows them twice, Overview once more, and '· ms' appears in the title and in both legend entries.
issues.fix: State the interaction hint once per page, for example in the KPI explanation strip or as a tooltip on the chart title, and keep only data-specific notes under each chart. Put the unit in the title only ('Duration trend · ms') and drop it from the legend labels.

issues.element: Durations show as 2,400 / 1,100 ms and the axis runs 0–4,000 ms. Values in seconds are easier to read as '2.4 s'.
issues.fix: Format durations of 1,000 ms or more as seconds with one decimal ('2.4 s'), and use ms below that, consistently across KPIs, axes, tables and breakdown bars.

issues.element: Duration tiles say 'Unavailable / No range total', but a p95 or a mean is not a total. Charts say 'No measured values in this interval.' with no reason, and 'View data table' is still offered under charts that have no values.
issues.fix: Use 'Not measured in this range' plus the reason (for example 'durations not recorded by this source'). Hide 'View data table' when a chart has no rows.

issues.element: The pager shows 'Page 1' under 3 rows while the header says '128 retained events'. There is no page count or row range. Cell captions 'Usage presence reported', 'Unavailable / Unpriced' and 'Explicit zero rate' are internal jargon, and the 'Details' column header repeats the button label.
issues.fix: Show 'Rows 1–3 of 128' next to the pager. Rename captions to plain words ('Tokens reported', 'Not priced', 'Rate set to $0'). Leave the Details column header blank, or make it a visually hidden label.

issues.element: The time-range pills, bucket pills and 'Current bucket: hour' stay active on a tab whose note says 'These are not historical rates'. The amber 'Model catalog unavailable for Offline synthetic source' warning gives no next step, and 'Offline' is capitalised mid-sentence.
issues.fix: Disable or hide time-range and bucket controls on Model Rates, with a short 'Rates are current; time range does not apply'. Reword the warning to 'Model catalog could not be loaded for the offline synthetic source, so the list may be incomplete. Refresh to retry.'

issues.element: With 0 events, Estimated cost and p95 duration say 'Unavailable / No range total', which reads as a measurement fault, not as no activity. 'Reported output tokens 0' has no caption while its neighbours do, and Failed events reads '0 / of 0 events'.
issues.fix: For zero-event ranges, show '$0.00' for cost and '—' with 'No events' for duration, give every tile a caption, and replace 'of 0 events' with 'No events'.

issues.element: Empty banner 'Choose a longer range to look further back.' offers no control. At 390, the range picker is hidden inside the collapsed 'Shared filters' disclosure.
issues.fix: Add an inline 'Show last 7 days' button to the banner that sets the range.

issues.element: 'The local analytics dataset is not configured or is temporarily unavailable. Check the server dataset binding, then retry.' hedges between two causes. Provider, model and outcome dropdowns stay enabled while Apply is disabled.
issues.fix: Name the specific cause when the server knows it, and give the setting or file to check. Disable the filter dropdowns in the error state to match Apply.

issues.element: Skeleton tiles are an improvement, but the chart skeleton text reads 'Loading analytics...' with three dots instead of an ellipsis, and the header loses the 'Partial coverage / Updated' meta, so the header height shifts when data arrives.
issues.fix: Use 'Loading analytics…' (U+2026), and reserve the header meta line with a placeholder so nothing jumps.

issues.element: Header meta: 'Partial coverage' is plain grey text at the same weight as the date range, although it is the main caveat on every number below.
issues.fix: Give 'Partial coverage' the amber warning ink plus a small warning icon, and merge it with the 'Coverage limitations' disclosure, for example '⚠ Partial coverage ▸'.

regressions: Tokens (all sizes): Cache-write and Reported reasoning flat sparklines are now grey, not violet. r13 used a 'Flat trend' note, and the new grey lines break the token = violet rule and read as placeholders.
Cost (all sizes): Priced and Unpriced events now show full-width flat grey lines, not the r13 'Flat trend' note. Grey is not the count ink (white), and the lines look like dividers.
reference_gaps: Below about 1366 px, Clear filters collapses to a bare × and the bucket readout disappears. The reference keeps labelled 'Clear all' and 'Current bucket' at all toolbar widths.

The reference has a refresh-status chip ('● (6s)') beside Refresh showing auto-refresh state. Prox shows only the Refresh button, with no last-refreshed or auto-refresh indicator in the toolbar (the 'Updated' time sits in the header instead).

The reference puts search on its own full-width row, with the filter dropdowns as an even 4-column row below. Prox squeezes search, Apply and three dropdowns into one row, so search is shorter and needs an extra Apply button the reference does not have.
The reference's filter set includes client API keys. Prox has providers, models and outcomes, but no client-key or credential filter (this may be intentional scope).
The reference has no time range or bucket controls on reference-only views. Prox keeps them active on Model Rates, where they have no effect.
